answer: Each agent must lock a slashable stake and collect vouchers from several distinct staked peers before its vote counts as the square root of that stake. Splitting a fortune across fake identities shrinks total root power, while every new identity still needs its own bond and fresh vouchers from unrelated agents. A gale of Sybil accounts therefore costs the attacker linearly in locked capital yet buys no extra sway: the meadow stays fair and the fabricated thread of trust snaps when slashing lands.
